source_title: Google's cheapest Gemini plan is losing a major perk; now I can't recommend it to anyone
source_excerpt:
Parth is a technology analyst and writer specializing in the comprehensive review and feature exploration of the Android ecosystem. His work focus on productivity apps and flagship devices, particularly Google Pixel and Samsung mobile hardware and software.
He provides expert guidance on productivity software, system optimization, and the advanced functionalities that allow users to maximize their device's potential. Google AI Plus has been one of the easiest ways to experience Gemini's more powerful features without spending a fortune.
It was a compelling middle ground for users who wanted more than the free version but couldn't justify paying for Google AI Pro.
Unfortunately, Google is about to make that deal less attractive, and now I am not sure if I can recommend it to everyone.
Google AI Plus was the sweet spot for budget-conscious users
The affordable Gemini sweet spot disappears
I have always felt that Google AI Plus struck the right balance between affordability and functionality.
Not everyone needs to spend $20 a month on an AI subscription, especially when most of us use chatbots for everyday tasks like drafting emails, summarizing documents, brainstorming ideas, or getting quick answers.
At $5 a month, Google AI Plus offered a compelling alternative.
What made it attractive to me was that it doesn't completely lock users out of Google's most powerful Pro models.
While the usage limits were lower than the expensive tiers, the option to switch to Pro for complex queries was a major advantage.
With 400GB of cloud storage, Deep Research, and extra AI features, the subscription felt like excellent value for money.
For someone who wanted more than the free Gemini experience without paying a premium, AI Plus seemed like the obvious choice.
Google is taking away an existing benefit
Flash is capable, but it doesn't replace Pro
What bothers me most about this change is that Google isn't simply reserving its upcoming AI models for more expensive subscriptions.
It's taking away a feature AI Plus subscribers could access.
I can understand Google wanting to give its premium subscribers higher usage limits and exclusive features.
After all, running powerful AI models isn't cheap. But removing an existing benefit from a paid plan is different.
Starting November 13, AI Plus subscribers will no longer be able to select Pro models in the Gemini app or AI Mode in Google Search.
To keep using those models, they will have to upgrade to the 4x more expensive AI Pro subscription.
And that's where I have a problem with Google's approach.
People signed up for AI Plus expecting to occasionally use Pro models, even if their usage was restricted.
Now they are being asked to pay more to keep something they already got.
Don't get me wrong, Google's Flash models are no slouch.
Gemini 3.8 Flash, in particular, has made impressive gains in reasoning, coding, and handling complex tasks.
For everyday activities, I would argue that a capable Flash model is more than enough for most people.
I am more concerned about what happens next.
As impressive as Gemini 3.8 Flash is, I expect Google's next-generation Pro model to push the boundaries further, especially when it comes to advanced reasoning, coding, and tackling complicated queries.
That's where I think AI Plus subscribers will start feeling the heat.
When Google releases a more capable Pro model, AI Plus subscribers will have to watch from the sidelines unless they upgrade.
Previously, they could experiment with Google's powerful models without committing to an expensive subscription.
That flexibility was one of the biggest reasons to consider AI Plus.
Losing it might not seem like much today, especially if Flash handles most of your tasks just fine. But as Google's Pro models keep improving, it could become a dealbreaker in the future.
AI Plus still has value, but its target audience is changing
Fast answers can't replace deeper thinking
Despite all my criticism, I wouldn't go so far as to call Google AI Plus a bad subscription. There is still plenty to like about it.
For starters, you get 400GB of cloud storage , access to additional features in Gemini Notebook, AI assistance in Gemini, and expanded access to Google's image and video generation tools.
And Gemini Flash remains available for everyday tasks.
However, I feel the type of user who would benefit most from this subscription is changing.
Previously, I could easily recommend AI Plus to someone who wanted to experiment with Google's AI models without spending too much money.
That recommendation is becoming much harder.
AI Plus is gradually starting to feel more like a cloud storage subscription with some AI perks bundled in, rather than an affordable gateway to Google's more powerful AI capabilities.
Google is creating a fragmented Gemini experience
Gemini's subscription maze keeps getting messier
Another thing that frustrates me about Google's approach is how complicated its Gemini subscriptions are becoming.
Keeping track of which models are available with which plans is already confusing, and these latest restrictions only make it worse.
Even within the Flash family, there is a distinction: AI Plus subscribers currently get Gemini 3.6 Flash in the Gemini app, while the newer 3.8 Flash is available on the Pro and Ultra plans.
The confusion expands to the other products. For example, I am on a Google AI Pro plan, and yet I don't have access to Gemini Argon in Antigravity.
I shouldn't have to dig through multiple support pages and subscription comparison charts to figure out which AI models I am paying for.
I understand Google wants to make its expensive AI subscriptions more attractive, but I don't think taking away existing benefits is the right approach.
AI Plus was a great entry point for anyone looking to explore Gemini's advanced capabilities without spending too much.
With Pro access disappearing, that appeal is fading.
